Lunar south pole · 89.5° S

South Pole Lander

Fly a powered descent to the connecting ridge beside Shackleton crater, where the Sun never rises more than 1.5° above the horizon. Engines, propellant, guidance and touchdown limits are modelled from published numbers where they exist.

Controls
AUTO: guidance flies. Redesignate the landing point by tapping the map (it zooms in below 4 km), with the arrow keys, or flicking the left stick. Safe site jumps to the nearest spot the hazard scan rates safe.
ROD, like Apollo's P66: you fly attitude with the rotational hand controller (RHC); the computer throttles to hold the rate of descent you set with the ROD switch, 0.3 m/s per click. Pressing the ROD switch in AUTO hands over.
MANUAL: RHC attitude, throttle lever, and the translational hand controller (THC) firing RCS.
Keyboard: WS pitch, AD roll, QE yaw · arrows THC (or LPD in AUTO) · R/F ROD slower/faster (THC up/down in MANUAL) · Shift/Ctrl throttle, X full, Z cut · T engines · 123 AUTO/ROD/MANUAL · H safe site
Gamepad: right stick RHC, bumpers yaw, left stick THC (LPD in AUTO), triggers throttle, d-pad ROD, A ROD · B AUTO · X MANUAL · Y camera. Flight sticks: stick RHC, twist yaw, slider throttle.
Camera: drag the scene to orbit or look around, pinch or scroll to zoom, double-tap to reset. C next view · IJKL orbit · U/O zoom · V reset
P pause · [/] time warp
What is modelled, and what is estimated
  • Point-mass flight in the Moon's central gravity field, with curvature, from a 15 × 100 km orbit. Attitude is rate-limited; throttles lag and cannot go below each engine's floor.
  • Starship HLS brakes on Raptors, then hands over to mid-body landing thrusters near the surface, because one Raptor at minimum throttle would still push a ~250 t lander upward at over 2 m/s². Thruster count and thrust are estimates.
  • Blue Moon MK2 flies three BE-7 hydrogen engines (44 kN, 460 s, 20–100% throttle, published). Its propellant load and geometry are estimates.
  • Guidance is an energy-optimal ZEM/ZEV law re-solved every step, flown through gates like Apollo's P63/P64/P66. If an engine failure leaves no landing solution, it aborts to orbit.
  • Sunlight is traced across the terrain for every vertex, including the Moon's curvature and the Sun's 0.53° disk. No atmosphere: black sky, no haze, dust flies on ballistic arcs.
  • Touchdown is judged on sink rate, drift, attitude, slope across the footpads, boulders under pads and tip-over margin from the centre-of-mass height.
